name: markdown-sections-as-symbols
body: Markdown headings must map to graph symbols, and every document must carry exactly one document-root section that anchors its whole-document and preamble links. Each heading becomes a Struct section symbol; each document also gets a single synthesized document-root section Struct — the document-level section representing the document as a whole and its non-heading body before the first heading. Containment is the section hierarchy under the file: the File contains the document-root Struct (File→Struct is a legal pair), the document-root contains every top-level heading, and every deeper heading is contained by the nearest preceding lower-level heading, else by the document-root (Struct→Struct). The schema nests symbols only through Struct, so a section is a Struct. The FQN scheme must be injective by construction, because the ingestor panics on any residual FQN collision rather than overwriting (SPEC §4). The scheme is anchored on the file's absolute path, never on a dot-joined directory/file-stem prefix: a markdown Module's FQN is the directory's absolute path; a markdown File's FQN is the file's absolute path, so the extension is retained and `docs/README.md` and `docs/README.markdown` are distinct; the document-root section's FQN is `<file-fqn>.<document-root-segment>`, where `<document-root-segment>` is a fixed reserved literal (e.g. `document-root`), not a slug of any heading text; a heading section's FQN extends its parent section's FQN as `<parent-section-fqn>.<section>`. Because the document-root is the only section at its depth and every heading FQN is strictly deeper (a heading always descends from the document-root), the document-root can never collide with a heading regardless of the slug rule, and absolute paths are unique per file, so module and file prefixes stay disjoint and no two files (or two directories) render to the same section FQN. Dot-joining a directory path is explicitly rejected as the lossy alternative that aliases `docs/guide` and `docs.guide` to the same `docs.guide` prefix. The exact slug rule that turns heading text into a name segment is a plan-time choice (see the open-points note); it must be delimiter-safe — a slug maps heading text to one segment and never embeds the `.` separator ambiguously — and must map duplicate headings in one file to distinct segments. The collision-freedom AC is testable now and independent of the exact slug rule: the same-stem files and the path-alias directories differ in their absolute-path prefix, and the document-root is strictly shallower than every heading regardless of the slug rule, so no AC outcome rests on a deferred slug decision. AC: a document with nested headings yields one Struct per heading plus its document-root Struct, each contained by the correct parent (a heading by the document-root or the nearest preceding lower-level heading); a document with no headings yields its document-root Struct and no heading Struct; the same-stem fixture (`docs/README.md` and `docs/README.markdown`, each with a `## Overview`) and the path-alias fixture (`docs/guide/x.md` and `docs.guide/x.md`) yield distinct section FQNs (disambiguated by their absolute-path prefixes, independent of the exact slug rule) and no ingestor FQN-collision panic.
